sights.w: Six floors of manga, anime, retro games, idol merch, cosplay and collectibles, vintage to new; Mandarake's Osaka flagship relocated from Amerikamura to Den Den Town in December 2020.
sights.anime: Mandarake — Osaka's flagship used-otaku megastore, the anchor of Den Den Town

sights.w: The retro-video-game specialist's only store outside Tokyo: shelves of Famicom/Super Famicom carts and consoles plus a retro arcade, on the Den Den Town strip.
sights.anime: Retro gaming — Super Potato, Japan's best-known retro game shop (Akihabara's twin)

sights.w: One of western Japan's largest official anime/manga goods stores, the Ota Road anchor; the same building holds Lashinbang, Melonbooks and card-game floors.
sights.anime: Animate — the official anime-goods chain's big Osaka store on Ota Road

sights.w: The drum-playing clown mascot (1950) of the long-closed Cui-daore restaurant (shut 2008), now greeting visitors at the renovated Nakaza Kuidaore Building on the old Nakaza theatre site — one of Dōtonbori's most-photographed icons.
sights.anime: Pop culture — Kuidaore Taro, Osaka's 'eat-till-you-drop' mascot since 1950

sights.w: 1956 Sennichimae leisure building whose 2nd-floor warren of tiny bars and the Misono Universe hall made it an Ura-Namba nightlife legend; tenants left at the end of 2024 and the whole building closed on 5 July 2025 ahead of redevelopment.
